Here’s a “Mindfulness Exercise” For You to Try!

One of the challenges and therefore hesitations we get from people is giving up alcohol, sugar and dairy while on the program.

The first thing we say is, "It's only for a short bubble of time and you can do ANYTHING for this short period!"

But there's still some hesitation. Once people are fully into the program and losing tons of weight and inches most are satisfied just going without these things. But at this point some may be tempted, thinking, "I've come so far, a glass of wine or piece of chocolate won't hurt anything...."

Well, here's a shocker for you: One beer is like eating half a loaf of bread! In fact, the way the liver processes alcohol is such that your body will not only stop burning abnormal fat but start storing the calories from alcohol as abnormal fat!  Yeah, think about that before taking even a sip.

Okay, we're about to suggest something really shocking right now: break the rules a little.

Choose something that you have been missing – either an alcoholic beverage or treat. We are going to play a little game with it. This game is a “mindfulness exercise.”

Whatever the food or drink you choose, take the first little sip or bite and just hold it in your mouth. You will likely feel a “rush” start to take over you. These are your brain’s “old habit” pathways that are going to make you want to devour it and more.  

RESIST the urge to swallow at that moment. 

Hold it in your mouth and watch as the “rush” starts to subside. Now, experience the taste of it on your tongue.

Do you even like it? Does it taste the same? I’ll bet it’s somehow different. That’s the transformation of your relationship with food and drink that is occurring within you on this program.  

Very Powerful!

Dr. Nicole

Something to think about after ChiroThin!

 

I wanted to share some amazing benefits of walking. Walking might seem simple, but trust me, it can work wonders for your weight loss journey! Here are some key points to consider:

Burns Calories: Walking is a low-impact aerobic exercise that helps burn calories and contributes to creating a calorie deficit, which is crucial for weight loss. Even a brisk walk for 30 minutes can burn a significant amount of calories.

Boosts Metabolism: Regular walking increases your metabolism, allowing your body to burn calories more efficiently even when you're not exercising. This means you'll continue to burn calories throughout the day, aiding in weight loss.

Supports Fat Loss: Walking, particularly at a moderate intensity, can help your body tap into its fat stores for energy. As a result, consistent walking can lead to fat loss and a leaner physique.

Enhances Muscle Tone: Walking engages various muscles in your body, including your legs, glutes, and core. Over time, this can lead to improved muscle tone, giving you a more sculpted appearance.

Reduces Stress and Appetite: Walking is a fantastic stress reliever. It releases endorphins, also known as "feel-good" hormones, which can help curb emotional eating and reduce cravings.

So, lace up your sneakers and take advantage of the wonderful benefits of walking! It's a simple, accessible, and enjoyable way to support your weight loss goals.

Remember, consistency is key! Try to incorporate walking into your daily routine and gradually increase your pace and duration.

Feel free to share your own experiences and let us know how walking has helped you on your weight loss journey!

 

A little exercise might be beneficial,

Where Does the Fat Go?

 

Most people find this surprising, but when you burn fat, it is converted into carbon dioxide and water. 

Current Research shows that during weight loss, 84 percent of the fat that is lost turns into carbon dioxide and leaves the body through the lungs, whereas the remaining 16 percent becomes water.

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part II

 

Yesterday we learned about fat burning and fat storage mode and how turning one on turns the other off – just like drive and reverse in your car – Reciprocal Inhibition. The day before that we talked about momentum.

Today, I want to put those two together and give you a “why” for a couple aspects of our program.

First, the eating pattern is a “2-8-16 pattern.” 2 Meals in 8 hours, followed by 16 hours of fasting. You must eat your entire meal in one sitting instead of spreading it out over several hours. As soon as you start to eat, your body signals to stop “Fat Burning” and start “Digesting.” After you have eaten, your body will process the food, extract the calories and use some of them and store some of them. When that is completed, it goes back into “fat burning” of your abnormal fat. If you didn’t eat your apple at lunch, for example, and saved it for 3pm, then what would happen? The fat burning stops and digestion starts and “halt” goes your fat burning momentum between meals. Ugh…!

What about sugar free gum and breath mints or even eating free veggies as a snack? The same effect occurs. The act of chewing causes digestive enzymes to be released in the mouth which triggers the stop “Fat Burning” command and that signals start “Fat Storage.” Of course, it is a false start because there are no “net” calories to extract, so it’s not like chewing gum will cause you to gain weight, but the loss of momentum is what hurts your weight loss progress and that’s what we want to avoid.

If you feel you need to snack, drink some water, get busy on something for ten minutes and see if you still need that snack – normally the urge will be gone. Remember the CRuSH Technique as well….

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part I

Remember, there is no cheating on the program. As soon as you cheat, you lose momentum and throw yourself into a stall.

Reciprocal inhibition is a fancy scientific term. I will give you an example of reciprocal inhibition – when you have your car in “Reverse” it can’t be in “Drive” at the same time.  In the body, when you flex your bicep muscle, the triceps muscle will relax –that’s reciprocal inhibition. 

What the heck does this have to do with weight loss? Well, absolutely everything!

Reciprocal inhibition plays a part in fat burning and fat storage just like the transmission in your car. When you are in fat storage mode, you won’t be burning fat. And when your body is in fat burning mode, you can’t store it.

The foods you are eating on our plan in combination with the eating pattern and the ChiroThin drops and supplements puts you in FAT BURNING MODE. As soon as you stray from the program, fat burning stops. 

Eating your normal meal of 4 oz of protein, 4 oz of both vegetables and fruit will stop the fat burning process temporarily and for good reason. Your body will use the calories from your meal to replenish your reserve fat stores. That is necessary because those reserves are what runs your body overnight.  But as soon as they are used up, the body goes back into burning your abnormal fat stores which is the fat we don’t want!

Keep burning!

Dr. Nicole

Do you feel hungry?

Going on a very low-calorie diet may be a bit of a shock for some people.  Most of us are used to eating all the time and way more than we need.  Learning to only eat small quantities can be tough.  The ChiroThin drops and support products will help keep your appetite at bay for the most part, and soon you’ll probably find that you will have a hard time eating all the food at each meal, but in the early days, it might be hard.

Here are some tips to help you out!

  • Add free vegetables to your meal in the form of a salad
  • Add free vegetables to your main course, like a stir fry using red cabbage, peppers, onions and celery
  • Have a few pickles or tomatoes with your meal.
  • Heat up some sauerkraut & green peppers with garlic, and pepper as a warm side dish
  • Have a bowl of “Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup with your meal

”Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup

  • 3 Red Bell Peppers – Cored and sectioned
  • ½ Purple Onion – cut in large chunks
  • 3 Cloves of Fresh Garlic
  • Can of Organic Diced Tomatoes
  • Water and Zero Calorie Non-Stick Cooking Spray 
  • Dried Basil
  • Dried Rosemary
  • Pink Himalayan Salt 
  • Boiling Water

Toss red peppers, onions and garlic with Cooking Spray, Basil and Rosemary. Sprinkle with salt and roast in oven for 25 minutes at 425 degrees F.  Do not let vegetables blacken from the high heat, so turn often. When sufficiently roasted, remove from the oven and put in a high powered blender.  Add one can of diced tomatoes and boiling water.  Blend at high speed for about a minute.  

*Cooking alternative – instead of roasting, cook vegetables in a wok on the stove. It’s quicker and just as tasty!

Get creative with your food and have fun.  The variety will help you enjoy losing weight and there is never any reason to be hungry on this program.  But keep in mind, eating anything that isn’t on the approved foods list will cause hunger and cravings.  If in doubt, leave it out!

Use the Recipe search feature on the ChiroThinTracker app to find great plan approved recipes – you can mark them as “Favorite” and print them as well. 

Reminder: This is not a no salt, no seasoning diet! See page 25 in the ChiroThin Instruction Manual for approved sauces and seasonings. It’s best to not get “bored” with your food choices!

Let’s talk about nutrition labels. Do you know how to read them?

 

Some people think they know, others only focus on one area and some people have never even given the nutrition label anything more than a glance!

We don’t count calories on the plan, we weigh our food, as you know, but calories are listed on the label. The biggest misconception in the “diet” industry is that a calorie equals a calorie. This has never been true, is not true and will never be true. One calorie from alcohol and one calorie from ice cream and one calorie from chicken breast are all handled differently in the body and are therefore, not equal. If they were, you could only drink whiskey, eat no food and be totally healthy!

 

Let me walk you through how to read the label and why it's vital to your success both now and in the future.

  1. Nutrition Facts
    • Start here: One of the most important steps, note the size of a single serving and how many servings are in a package. This tricks a lot of people. You may think a single drink or packaged food item is of course one serving, but many times there are many servings in one package. This can add up to disaster for you!
  2. Calories
    • Check total calories per serving: Look at the serving size and how many servings you're really consuming. If you double the servings you eat, you double the calories and nutrients, including the Percent Daily Value (% DV). Always do the math!
  3. Total Fat/Carbohydrates/Protein
    • Fat: Remember, you need to limit your total fat to no more than 56-78 grams a day — including no more than 16 grams of saturated fat, less than two grams of trans fat, and less than 300 mg cholesterol (these are all based on a 2,000-calorie diet).  On the ChiroThin Program you need to eat far less – fat to protein ratio is 7% fat to 93% protein – that’s 93% lean protein. It is possible to do the calculations using the ingredient label, but you would need to know that 1 gram of protein provides 4 calories and, but 1 gram of fat provides 9 calories. For information’s sake, 1 gram of carbohydrate provides 4 calories.
  4. % Daily Value
    • Quick guide to % DV: The % DV section tells you the percent of each nutrient in a single serving, in terms of the daily-recommended amount. As a guide, if you want to consume less of a nutrient (such as saturated fat, cholesterol or sodium), choose foods with a lower % DV — 5 percent or less is low. If you want to consume more of a nutrient (such as fiber), seek foods with a higher % DV — 20 percent or more is high.

 

Remember that the information shown in these panels is based on 2,000 calories a day. That’s about 3 times more food than you are eating now.  The number of calories you require once you’ve reached your desired weight will be based upon your gender, age, height and weight.  For a 45-year-old male measuring 5’9” and 170 pounds doing light exercise 1-3 times a week would require about 2000 calories a day.  However, a 50-year-old female measuring 5’5” weighing 155 pounds doing little to no exercise would only require 1400 a day. 

 

I can't stress enough the importance of reading and understanding nutrition labels. They are often confusing and made that way intentionally. It's important you understand how to read them and take control of what enters your body.

 

For the ingredients label, remember items are listed in order of amount. The product contains more of the first ingredient listed than the last ingredient listed. Just for fun, next time you are in the grocery store, go to some of the foods you used to eat and see what ingredient are listed first.  Sugar? High fructose corn syrup? Might be surprising to you….

 

Happy, healthy eating!

Yesterday you learned about fat burning and fat storage mode and how turning one on turns the other off – just like drive and reverse in your car – Reciprocal Inhibition. The day before that I talked about momentum.

 

Today, I want to put those two together and give you a “why” for a couple aspects of our program.

 

First, the eating pattern is a “2-8-16 pattern.” 2 Meals in 8 hours, followed by 16 hours of fasting. You must eat your entire meal in one sitting instead of spreading it out over several hours. As soon as you start to eat, your body signals to stop “Fat Burning” and start “Digesting.” After you have eaten, your body will process the food, extract the calories and use some of them and store some of them. When that is completed, it goes back into “fat burning” of your abnormal fat. If you didn’t eat your apple at lunch, for example, and saved it for 3pm, then what would happen? The fat burning stops and digestion starts and “halt” goes your fat burning momentum between meals. Ugh…!

 

What about sugar free gum and breath mints or even eating free veggies as a snack? The same effect occurs. The act of chewing causes digestive enzymes to be released in the mouth which triggers the stop “Fat Burning” command and that signals start “Fat Storage.” Of course, it is a false start because there are no “net” calories to extract, so it’s not like chewing gum will cause you to gain weight, but the loss of momentum is what hurts your weight loss progress and that’s what we want to avoid.

 

If you feel you need to snack, drink some water, get busy on something for ten minutes and see if you still need that snack – normally the urge will be gone.

 

You’re doing great!

Reciprocal inhibition is a fancy scientific term. I will give you an example of reciprocal inhibition – when you have your car in “Reverse” it can’t be in “Drive” at the same time.  In the body, when you flex your bicep muscle, the triceps muscle will relax –that’s reciprocal inhibition.

 

What the heck does this have to do with weight loss? Well, absolutely everything!

 

Reciprocal inhibition plays a part in fat burning and fat storage just like the transmission in your car. When you are in fat storage mode, you won’t be burning fat. And when your body is in fat burning mode, you can’t store it.

 

The foods you are eating on our plan in combination with the eating pattern and supplement regimen puts you in FAT BURNING MODE. As soon as you stray from the program, fat burning stops.

 

Eating your normal meal of 4oz protein, 4oz or both vegetables and fruit will stop the fat burning process temporarily and for good reason. Your body will use the calories from your meal to replenish your reserve fat stores. That is necessary because those reserves are what runs your body over-night.  But as soon as they are used up, the body goes back into burning your abnormal fat stores which is the fat we don’t want

Keep burning!

Going on a low-calorie diet may be a bit of a shock for some people.  Most of us are used to eating all the time and way more than we need.  Learning to only eat small quantities can be tough.  The drops and support products will help keep your appetite at bay for the most part, and soon you’ll probably find that you will have a hard time eating all the food at each meal, but in the early days, it might be hard.

Dr. Chris’s “Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup

  • 3 Red Bell Peppers – Cored and sectioned
  • ½ Purple Onion – cut in large chunks
  • 3 Cloves of Fresh Garlic
  • Can of Organic Diced Tomatoes
  • Water and Zero Calorie Non-Stick Cooking Spray
  • Dried Basil
  • Dried Rosemary
  • Pink Himalayan Salt 
  • Boiling Water

 

Toss red peppers, onions and garlic with Cooking Spray, Basil and Rosemary. Sprinkle with salt and roast in oven for 25 minutes at 425 degrees F.  Do not let vegetables blacken from the high heat, so turn often. When sufficiently roasted, remove from oven and put in high powered blender.  Add one can of diced tomatoes and boiling water.  Blend at high speed for about a minute.  

 

*Cooking alternative – instead of roasting, cook vegetables in a wok on the stove. It’s quicker and just as tasty!

Day 36: Losing Phase

Let’s Talk Nutrition Labels!        

 

Let’s talk about nutrition labels. Do you know how to read them?

 

Some people think they know, others only focus on one area and some people have never even given the nutrition label anything more than a glance!

While on the program, you really don’t need to be considering most labels because you are only eating from the approved foods list and are mostly fresh, whole foods. We don’t count calories on the plan, we weigh our food, as you know, but calories are listed on the label. The biggest misconception in the “diet” industry is that a calorie equals a calorie. This has never been true, is not true and will never be true. One calorie from alcohol and one calorie from ice cream and one calorie from chicken breast are all handled differently in the body and are therefore, not equal. If they were, you could only drink whiskey, eat no food and be totally healthy!

Let’s walk you through how to read the label and why it's vital to your success both now and in the future.

  1. Nutrition Facts
    • Start here: One of the most important steps, note the size of a single serving and how many servings are in a package. This tricks a lot of people. You may think a single drink or packaged food item is of course one serving, but many times there are many servings in one package. This can add up to disaster for you!
  2. Calories
    • Check total calories per serving: Look at the serving size and how many servings you're really consuming. If you double the servings you eat, you double the calories and nutrients, including the Percent Daily Value (% DV). Always do the math!
  3. Total Fat/Carbohydrates/Protein
    • Fat: Remember, you need to limit your total fat to no more than 56-78 grams a day — including no more than 16 grams of saturated fat, less than two grams of trans fat, and less than 300 mg cholesterol (these are all based on a 2,000 calorie diet).  On the ChiroThin Program you need to eat far less – fat to protein ratio is 7% fat to 93% protein – that’s 93% lean protein. It is possible to do the calculations using the ingredient label, but you would need to know that 1 gram of protein provides 4 calories and but 1 gram of fat provides 9 calories. For information sake, 1 gram of carbohydrate provides 4 calories.
  4. % Daily Value
    • Quick guide to % DV: The % DV section tells you the percent of each nutrient in a single serving, in terms of the daily-recommended amount. As a guide, if you want to consume less of a nutrient (such as saturated fat, cholesterol or sodium), choose foods with a lower % DV — 5 percent or less is low. If you want to consume more of a nutrient (such as fiber), seek foods with a higher % DV — 20 percent or more is high.

Remember that the information shown in these panels is based on 2,000 calories a day. That’s about 4 times more food than you are eating now.  The number of calories you require once you’ve reached your desired weight will be based upon your gender, age, height and weight.  For a 45-year-old male measuring 5’9” and 170 pounds doing light exercise 1-3 times a week would require about 2000 calories a day.  However, a 50-year-old female measuring 5’5” weighing 155 pounds doing little to no exercise would only require 1400 a day. 

We can't stress enough the importance of reading and understanding nutrition labels. They are often confusing and made that way intentionally. It's important you understand how to read them and take control of what enters your body.

For the ingredients label, remember items are listed in order of amount. The product contains more of the first ingredient listed than the last ingredient listed. Just for fun, next time you are in the grocery store, go to some of the foods you used to eat and see what ingredient are listed first.  Sugar? High fructose corn syrup? Might be surprising to you….

 

Happy, healthy eating!

Dr. Doug Brewer

Where Does the Fat Go?

 

Most people find this surprising, but when you burn fat, it is converted into carbon dioxide and water.

 

Current Research shows that during weight loss, 84 percent of the fat that is lost turns into carbon dioxide and leaves the body through the lungs, whereas the remaining 16 percent becomes water.

 

That means the lungs are the primary excretory organ for weight loss. The water formed may be excreted in the urine, feces, sweat, breath, tears or other bodily fluids.

If you aren’t, start adding water every day to hit the minimum 80oz – 120 oz goal over the next week and a half or two weeks. Water is very important, but too much of anything can create problems!

AHHHH ASPARAGUS

The Health Benefits of Asparagus

This giant veggie is one of the most nutritionally well-balanced vegetables -- high in folic acid and a good source of potassium, fiber, thiamin, and vitamins A, B6, and C. A 5-ounce serving provides 60% of the RDA for folic acid and is low in calories.

Doctors Favorite Asparagus Recipe

Clean and trim woody ends from asparagus stalks

Prepare air fryer or regular oven with directions below

In an air fryer use the french-fry setting (15 minutes at 400)

Spray the cooking grate with Pam spray

In oven, set temperature for 400

Line a baking sheet with parchment paper

Place asparagus in a single layer on cooking surface

Lightly spray asparagus with Pam spray

Season with Lemon Pepper seasoning or simply salt

Bake for 15 minutes

For a fresh kick, squeeze fresh lemon on asparagus just before serving

SLEEP AND WEIGHT LOSS

This ongoing topic of self-care is always super important.  We mentioned sleep yesterday but today we will dive a little deeper

 

According to health.gov, here are some benefits of proper sleep.

The Basics: Health Benefits

  1. Sleep helps reduce stress

If your body doesn’t get enough sleep, it can react by producing an elevated level of stress hormones, which are a natural result of today’s fast-paced lifestyles.  Deep and regular sleep can help prevent this

  1.  Sleep can improve your memory

 

Ever noticed that when you’re really tired it’s harder to remember things? Basically, this is your brain telling you that it’s not getting enough sleep. When you sleep well, your body may be resting but your brain is busy organizing and storing memories. So getting more quality sleep will help you remember and process things better.

 

  1. Sleep can lower your blood pressure

 

Higher blood pressure increases your chances of heart attacks and strokes, but getting plenty of restful sleep encourages a constant state of relaxation that can help reduce blood pressure and generally keep it under control.

 

  1. Sleep helps your body to fight back

 

While you’re sleeping your body is producing extra protein molecules that can strengthen your ability to fight infections. If you’re feeling a bit run down and don’t want it to turn into a full-blown cold, go to bed early and get lots of rest.

     5. Sleep can help you maintain your weight

Unfortunately, sleep won’t directly make you lose weight, but it can help you keep it under control by regulating the hormones that affect your appetite and reducing your cravings for high calorie foods.

6. Sleep puts you in a better mood

Lack of sleep can make us more agitated, so we’re more likely to snap at our boss or be grumpy with a loved one – neither of which is a good thing. The better you sleep, the better your ability to stay calm, controlled and reasonable.

7. Sleep could reduce your chances of diabetes

Some research studies have shown that not getting enough sleep may lead to type 2 diabetes by affecting how your body processes glucose. It’s not conclusive by any means, but it’s yet another indication of how important the benefits of sleep can be.

8. Sleep helps keep your heart healthy

A regular sleep pattern can help to lower the levels of stress and inflammation to your cardiovascular system, which in turn can reduce your chances of a heart condition.

9. Sleep can be a painkiller

If you’re suffering pain from a recent injury like a sprained ankle, getting plenty of sleep can actually make it hurt less. Many studies have shown a link between sleep loss and a lower pain threshold. Basically the more sleep you get, the less pain you might be in.

10. Sleep can make you smarter

Along with a great night’s sleep, grabbing a quick nap in the daytime can contribute towards making your brain more effective and productive. You won’t necessarily be answering all the questions on University Challenge, but you may well feel sharper, more attentive, and focused throughout the day.

If you’ve ever thought that sleep doesn’t matter all that much, think again, because it actually matters a great deal.

Sleep definitely has a huge impact on your health and wellbeing.  If you have difficulty sleeping, try some of these things…

  • Keep a regular bedtime and rising time.
  • Stay off of electronic devices at least one hour prior to bedtime.
  • Prepare yourself for the next day ahead of time to allow your mind to relax at night.
  • 30 minutes of reading or meditation prior to bedtime can help you fall asleep faster.
  • Sleep hypnosis helps many people.
  • Stop drinking caffeinated beverages early in the day
  • Start and end your day with gratitude.  Think about the good things in your life and how thankful you are for them.
  • Create a restful environment – fresh clean bedding, lavender oil, dim lighting, clean refreshing bedroom with everything in its place, etc.
  • Physical activity in your day also helps you sleep easier at night.
  • Keep a notepad next to your bed to write down those random thoughts that you may need to take care of the next day rather than continuing to keep those things on your mind.

 

If you have difficulty sleeping, sometimes melatonin helps many people fall and stay asleep.  It is all-natural and you can find it in many stores.  Check with your physician if you feel you may need something stronger for sleep disorders.

Let’s Talk Nutrition Labels!         

 

Let’s talk about nutrition labels. Do you know how to read them?

Some people think they know, others only focus on one area and some people have never even given the nutrition label anything more than a glance!

While on the program, you really don’t need to be considering most labels because you are only eating from the approved foods list and are mostly fresh, whole foods. We don’t count calories on the plan, we weigh our food, as you know, but calories are listed on the label. The biggest misconception in the “diet” industry is that a calorie equals a calorie. This has never been true, is not true and will never be true. One calorie from alcohol and one calorie from ice cream and one calorie from chicken breast are all handled differently in the body and are therefore, not equal. If they were, you could only drink whiskey, eat no food and be totally healthy!

Let’s walk you through how to read the label and why it's vital to your success both now and in the future.

  1. Nutrition Facts
    • Start here: One of the most important steps, note the size of a single serving and how many servings are in a package. This tricks a lot of people. You may think a single drink or packaged food item is of course one serving, but many times there are many servings in one package. This can add up to disaster for you!
  2. Calories
    • Check total calories per serving: Look at the serving size and how many servings you're really consuming. If you double the servings you eat, you double the calories and nutrients, including the Percent Daily Value (% DV). Always do the math!
  3. Total Fat/Carbohydrates/Protein
    • Fat: Remember, you need to limit your total fat to no more than 56-78 grams a day — including no more than 16 grams of saturated fat, less than two grams of trans fat, and less than 300 mg cholesterol (these are all based on a 2,000 calorie diet).  On the SlenderPro Program you need to eat far less – fat to protein ratio is 7% fat to 93% protein – that’s 93% lean protein. It is possible to do the calculations using the ingredient label, but you would need to know that 1 gram of protein provides 4 calories and but 1 gram of fat provides 9 calories. For information sake, 1 gram of carbohydrate provides 4 calories.
  4. % Daily Value
    • Quick guide to % DV: The % DV section tells you the percent of each nutrient in a single serving, in terms of the daily-recommended amount. As a guide, if you want to consume less of a nutrient (such as saturated fat, cholesterol or sodium), choose foods with a lower % DV — 5 percent or less is low. If you want to consume more of a nutrient (such as fiber), seek foods with a higher % DV — 20 percent or more is high.

Remember that the information shown in these panels is based on 2,000 calories a day. That’s about 4 times more food than you are eating now.  The number of calories you require once you’ve reached your desired weight will be based upon your gender, age, height and weight.  For a 45-year-old male measuring 5’9” and 170 pounds doing light exercise 1-3 times a week would require about 2000 calories a day.  However, a 50-year-old female measuring 5’5” weighing 155 pounds doing little to no exercise would only require 1400 a day. 

We can't stress enough the importance of reading and understanding nutrition labels. They are often confusing and made that way intentionally. It's important you understand how to read them and take control of what enters your body.

For the ingredients label, remember items are listed in order of amount. The product contains more of the first ingredient listed than the last ingredient listed. Just for fun, next time you are in the grocery store, go to some of the foods you used to eat and see what ingredient are listed first.  Sugar? High fructose corn syrup? Might be surprising to you….

 

Happy, healthy eating!

Where Does the Fat Go?

 

Most people find this surprising, but when you burn fat, it is converted into carbon dioxide and water.

 

Current Research shows that during weight loss, 84 percent of the fat that is lost turns into carbon dioxide and leaves the body through the lungs, whereas the remaining 16 percent becomes water.

 

That means the lungs are the primary excretory organ for weight loss. The water formed may be excreted in the urine, feces, sweat, breath, tears or other bodily fluids.

 

Keep breathing and have a great day!

Variety is the Spice of Life

 

While we have a few vegetarians participate in our program most are meat eaters. Meat provides protein and protein provides amino acids – amino acids are the building blocks of life. It is very important to get your amino acids from a wide variety of different meats.

 

As you move into month two of the program, you will likely notice your daily weight loss slowing down gradually. This is normal, albeit not as much fun as the first week or two. More, now than ever, it is paramount that you change up your protein source constantly. The last thing you want to do is eat the same protein 4 meals in a row!

 

If you eat chicken breast for lunch on Monday, try not to eat chicken breast again until at least Wednesday. It’s ok to have red meat, too, but change up the cuts. For example, if you have sirloin on Monday, it is ok to have filet mignon on Tuesday. Mix in some wild caught fish as well – but, remember, Salmon steaks are not allowed, but smoked salmon is ok. Tuna steaks are not allowed, but Tuna packed in water is ok.

 

Vary your fruits and vegetables as well so you ensure a wide variety of vitamins and minerals from your diet. You are eating for life – make it fun and make it delicious!

Only Weigh Once a Day!

 

Are you one of those people who are constantly checking their weight? If so, I’ll take a line out of Bob Newheart’s book and tell you to, “Stop It!”

 

Only weigh yourself once a day – first thing in the morning. That is the most consistent time to weigh – right when you wake up and after you go to the bathroom wearing the same thing, or preferably, nothing.

 

Weighing at night will frustrate you because it will be higher than in the morning. Your body took some of the calories you consumed to replenish your reserve fat so you can survive overnight. You fast when you sleep, but your body still requires energy in the form of calories. It gets those calories from your reserve fat. Breathing, blood pumping, healing, dreaming all take biological fuel (ATP) that comes from the conversion of fat to glucose.

 

Most people will burn anywhere from 1-5 pounds of reserve fat overnight. So only weigh in the morning and then log your daily submission into the SlenderProTracker and watch for our response.

 

The scale will go up, the scale will go down. Over the long run, it will be going down in a nice gradual slope.

Enjoy the process….

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part II

 

Yesterday we learned about fat burning and fat storage mode and how turning one on turns the other off – just like drive and reverse in your car – Reciprocal Inhibition. The day before that we talked about momentum.

 

Today, I want to put those two together and give you a “why” for a couple aspects of our program.

 

First, the eating pattern is a “2-8-16 pattern.” 2 Meals in 8 hours, followed by 16 hours of fasting. You must eat your entire meal in one sitting instead of spreading it out over several hours. As soon as you start to eat, your body signals to stop “Fat Burning” and start “Digesting.” After you have eaten, your body will process the food, extract the calories and use some of them and store some of them. When that is completed, it goes back into “fat burning” of your abnormal fat. If you didn’t eat your apple at lunch, for example, and saved it for 3pm, then what would happen? The fat burning stops and digestion starts and “halt” goes your fat burning momentum between meals. Ugh…!

 

What about sugar free gum and breath mints or even eating free veggies as a snack? The same effect occurs. The act of chewing causes digestive enzymes to be released in the mouth which triggers the stop “Fat Burning” command and that signals start “Fat Storage.” Of course, it is a false start because there are no “net” calories to extract, so it’s not like chewing gum will cause you to gain weight, but the loss of momentum is what hurts your weight loss progress and that’s what we want to avoid.

 

If you feel you need to snack, drink some water, get busy on something for ten minutes and see if you still need that snack – normally the urge will be gone. Remember the CRuSH Technique as well….

 

You’re doing great!

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part I

 

Reciprocal inhibition is a fancy scientific term. I will give you an example of reciprocal inhibition – when you have your car in “Reverse” it can’t be in “Drive” at the same time.  In the body, when you flex your bicep muscle, the triceps muscle will relax –that’s reciprocal inhibition.

 

What the heck does this have to do with weight loss? Well, absolutely everything!

 

Reciprocal inhibition plays a part in fat burning and fat storage just like the transmission in your car. When you are in fat storage mode, you won’t be burning fat. And when your body is in fat burning mode, you can’t store it.

 

The foods you are eating on our plan in combination with the eating pattern and the SlenderPro drops and supplements puts you in FAT BURNING MODE. As soon as you stray from the program, fat burning stops.

 

Eating your normal meal of 4oz protein, 4oz or both vegetables and fruit will stop the fat burning process temporarily and for good reason. Your body will use the calories from your meal to replenish your reserve fat stores. That is necessary because those reserves are what runs your body over-night.  But as soon as they are used up, the body goes back into burning your abnormal fat stores which is the fat we don’t want

Keep burning!

Going on a very low-calorie diet may be a bit of a shock for some people.  Most of us are used to eating all the time and way more than we need.  Learning to only eat small quantities can be tough.  The SlenderPro drops and support products will help keep your appetite at bay for the most part, and soon you’ll probably find that you will have a hard time eating all the food at each meal, but in the early days, it might be hard.

Here are some tips to help you out!

  • Add free vegetables to your meal in the form of a salad
  • Add free vegetables to your main course, like a stir fry using red cabbage, peppers, onions and celery
  • Have a few pickles or tomatoes with your meal.
  • Heat up some sauerkraut & green peppers with garlic, and pepper as a warm side dish
  • Have a bowl of Your SlenderPro Team’s “Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup with your meal

Your SlenderPro Team’s “Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup

  • 3 Red Bell Peppers – Cored and sectioned
  • ½ Purple Onion – cut in large chunks
  • 3 Cloves of Fresh Garlic
  • Can of Organic Diced Tomatoes
  • Water and Zero Calorie Non-Stick Cooking Spray
  • Dried Basil
  • Dried Rosemary
  • Pink Himalayan Salt 
  • Boiling Water

Toss red peppers, onions and garlic with Cooking Spray, Basil and Rosemary. Sprinkle with salt and roast in oven for 25 minutes at 425 degrees F.  Do not let vegetables blacken from the high heat, so turn often. When sufficiently roasted, remove from oven and put in high powered blender.  Add one can of diced tomatoes and boiling water.  Blend at high speed for about a minute.  

*Cooking alternative – instead of roasting, cook vegetables in a wok on the stove. It’s quicker and just as tasty!

Get creative with your food and have fun.  The variety will help you enjoy losing weight and there is never any reason to be hungry on this program.  But keep in mind, eating anything that isn’t on the approved foods list will cause hunger and cravings.  If in doubt, leave it out!

Do I have to eat all my food?

One of the most surprising questions I get is, “Do I have to eat all my food?” The answer is “YES!” People think they need to starve themselves to lose weight. Not true. On this program, you are eating a pound and a half of highly nutritious, nutrient dense food every day (plus all the free veggies you want!) If you think that skipping a meal or a meal component will result in more weight loss on the scale tomorrow morning, you will be unpleasantly surprised, most of the time. When you eat less than the prescribed daily allotment, your brain will over-ride the fat burning mode and put you into hard core storage mode because it thinks you are starving. Starvation mode is not the goal. Safe, rapid burning of your abnormal mode is the goal and is what will happen when you follow the plan.

So often we humans feel we can do things better by changing the plan. Please don’t do that with this program. Success leaves clues. Just do the little things every day and don’t stray. What could be easier?

It’s funny, but not surprising, how the people who stray from the plan don’t get the same results as the ones who just follow it. Trust me, I have a hard time with this because I am one of those who will challenge everything I am told. I have done that with this program and challenged it in every way imaginable. Guess what? It didn’t work as well as when I just followed it.

Please learn from our mistakes!

One question we get about water, “Is it possible to drink too much water?” The answer is yes. If you almost never drink water, then suddenly going to 120oz a day may cause problems – like stripping out your minerals – and you may start cramping.  If you are used to drinking water daily, then go ahead and increase your intake to 80 oz minimum. If you aren’t, start adding water every day to hit the minimum 80oz – 120 oz goal over the next week and a half or two weeks. Water is very important, but too much of anything can create problems!

One other question we get a lot after people read the SlenderPro manual is about oils, lotions and makeup. Check out the Resources tab of the SlenderProTracker for a comprehensive list of all approved oils and lotions. Oils, in general, interfere with the drops, so try to avoid them, both on your skin and on your food.

  • Kallikrein has a big job. It starts a process which includes proteins which opens your blood vessels to receive the nutrients you are swallowing.

The Health Benefits of Asparagus

This giant veggie is one of the most nutritionally well-balanced vegetables -- high in folic acid and a good source of potassium, fiber, thiamin, and vitamins A, B6, and C. A 5-ounce serving provides 60% of the RDA for folic acid and is low in calories.

Doctors Favorite Asparagus Recipe

Clean and trim woody ends from asparagus stalks

Prepare air fryer or regular oven with directions below

In an air fryer use the french-fry setting (15 minutes at 400)

Spray the cooking grate with Pam spray

In oven, set temperature for 400

Line a baking sheet with parchment paper

Place asparagus in a single layer on cooking surface

Lightly spray asparagus with Pam spray

Season with Lemon Pepper seasoning or simply salt

Bake for 15 minutes

For a fresh kick, squeeze fresh lemon on asparagus just before serving

SLEEP AND WEIGHT LOSS

This ongoing topic of self-care is always super important.  We mentioned sleep yesterday but today we will dive a little deeper

According to health.gov, here are some benefits of proper sleep.

The Basics: Health Benefits

  1. Sleep helps reduce stress

If your body doesn’t get enough sleep, it can react by producing an elevated level of stress hormones, which are a natural result of today’s fast-paced lifestyles.  Deep and regular sleep can help prevent this

  1.  Sleep can improve your memory

Ever noticed that when you’re really tired it’s harder to remember things? Basically, this is your brain telling you that it’s not getting enough sleep. When you sleep well, your body may be resting but your brain is busy organizing and storing memories. So getting more quality sleep will help you remember and process things better.

  1. Sleep can lower your blood pressure

Higher blood pressure increases your chances of heart attacks and strokes, but getting plenty of restful sleep encourages a constant state of relaxation that can help reduce blood pressure and generally keep it under control.

  1. Sleep helps your body to fight back

While you’re sleeping your body is producing extra protein molecules that can strengthen your ability to fight infections. If you’re feeling a bit run down and don’t want it to turn into a full-blown cold, go to bed early and get lots of rest.

     5. Sleep can help you maintain your weight

Unfortunately, sleep won’t directly make you lose weight, but it can help you keep it under control by regulating the hormones that affect your appetite and reducing your cravings for high calorie foods.

6. Sleep puts you in a better mood

Lack of sleep can make us more agitated, so we’re more likely to snap at our boss or be grumpy with a loved one – neither of which is a good thing. The better you sleep, the better your ability to stay calm, controlled and reasonable.

7. Sleep could reduce your chances of diabetes

Some research studies have shown that not getting enough sleep may lead to type 2 diabetes by affecting how your body processes glucose. It’s not conclusive by any means, but it’s yet another indication of how important the benefits of sleep can be.

8. Sleep helps keep your heart healthy

A regular sleep pattern can help to lower the levels of stress and inflammation to your cardiovascular system, which in turn can reduce your chances of a heart condition.

9. Sleep can be a painkiller

If you’re suffering pain from a recent injury like a sprained ankle, getting plenty of sleep can actually make it hurt less. Many studies have shown a link between sleep loss and a lower pain threshold. Basically the more sleep you get, the less pain you might be in.

10. Sleep can make you smarter

Along with a great night’s sleep, grabbing a quick nap in the daytime can contribute towards making your brain more effective and productive. You won’t necessarily be answering all the questions on University Challenge, but you may well feel sharper, more attentive, and focused throughout the day.

If you’ve ever thought that sleep doesn’t matter all that much, think again, because it actually matters a great deal.

Sleep definitely has a huge impact on your health and wellbeing.  If you have difficulty sleeping, try some of these things…

  • Keep a regular bedtime and rising time.
  • Stay off of electronic devices at least one hour prior to bedtime.
  • Prepare yourself for the next day ahead of time to allow your mind to relax at night.
  • 30 minutes of reading or meditation prior to bedtime can help you fall asleep faster.
  • Sleep hypnosis helps many people.
  • Stop drinking caffeinated beverages early in the day
  • Start and end your day with gratitude.  Think about the good things in your life and how thankful you are for them.
  • Create a restful environment – fresh clean bedding, lavender oil, dim lighting, clean refreshing bedroom with everything in its place, etc.
  • Physical activity in your day also helps you sleep easier at night.
  • Keep a notepad next to your bed to write down those random thoughts that you may need to take care of the next day rather than continuing to keep those things on your mind.

If you have difficulty sleeping, sometimes melatonin helps many people fall and stay asleep.  It is all-natural and you can find it in many stores.  Check with your physician if you feel you may need something stronger for sleep disorders.

Here’s a “Mindfulness Exercise” For You to Try!

RESIST the urge to swallow at that moment.

Hold it in your mouth and watch as the “rush” starts to subside. Now, experience the taste of it on your tongue.

Locking Phase

Nice work! Your losing phase is now complete and so you will no longer be taking any drops. Congratulations! You are now ready to begin locking in your weight and your new basal metabolic rate!

Please review the locking phase video on the website, under the Training tab.

The purpose of the locking in process is to establish your new “metabolic set point” and that will help you stay at your new weight. It normally takes between 3 and 5 weeks to accomplish this goal but it is well worth the effort.

During the locking phase you will experience a fair amount of fluctuations in your weight as your body finds its set point. Try not to get upset with your scale if your weight goes up a pound or two. It will go back down - as long as you stick to protocol. Most people will still lose 2-4 pounds on the locking phase.

From the standpoint of food choices, the locking phase is essentially the same as the losing phase. Do not add any foods to your diet that weren’t on the approved foods list, except for egg whites at breakfast. However, you will be eating greater quantities of food and adding breakfast as indicated below. Your body will adapt to its new Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) and once that is accomplished, your new weight will be locked in.

When you are ready to start your locking phase, discontinue taking drops. Then follow the same 4-4 and 4 pattern as on the losing phase for the three days. On the fourth day, you will add a small breakfast of lean protein and fruit. Things like turkey bacon or 2 egg whites and free vegetables to make an omelet are great choices. You can finish your breakfast with about 4 oz of fruit.

Lunch and dinner are the same as in the losing phase, but for women, you can have between 4.5-6 oz of each component and men can have between 5 and 8oz. As first it will seem like an awful lot of food.

You will want to keep drinking your water, keep taking your supplements as directed by your physician each day as you lock in your new set point.

It is very important for you to continue to log your daily weights on the weight loss tracker website/mobile app. Your weight will be locked in when it is within 1/2 a pound for 7 consecutive days and we will be watching this very closely.

Let’s Talk Nutrition Labels!         

Let’s talk about nutrition labels. Do you know how to read them?

Some people think they know, others only focus on one area and some people have never even given the nutrition label anything more than a glance!

While on the program, you really don’t need to be considering most labels because you are only eating from the approved foods list and are mostly fresh, whole foods. We don’t count calories on the plan, we weigh our food, as you know, but calories are listed on the label. The biggest misconception in the “diet” industry is that a calorie equals a calorie. This has never been true, is not true and will never be true. One calorie from alcohol and one calorie from ice cream and one calorie from chicken breast are all handled differently in the body and are therefore, not equal. If they were, you could only drink whiskey, eat no food and be totally healthy!

Let’s walk you through how to read the label and why it's vital to your success both now and in the future.

  1. Nutrition Facts
    • Start here: One of the most important steps, note the size of a single serving and how many servings are in a package. This tricks a lot of people. You may think a single drink or packaged food item is of course one serving, but many times there are many servings in one package. This can add up to disaster for you!
  2. Calories
    • Check total calories per serving: Look at the serving size and how many servings you're really consuming. If you double the servings you eat, you double the calories and nutrients, including the Percent Daily Value (% DV). Always do the math!
  3. Total Fat/Carbohydrates/Protein
    • Fat: Remember, you need to limit your total fat to no more than 56-78 grams a day — including no more than 16 grams of saturated fat, less than two grams of trans fat, and less than 300 mg cholesterol (these are all based on a 2,000 calorie diet).  On the SlenderPro Program you need to eat far less – fat to protein ratio is 7% fat to 93% protein – that’s 93% lean protein. It is possible to do the calculations using the ingredient label, but you would need to know that 1 gram of protein provides 4 calories and but 1 gram of fat provides 9 calories. For information sake, 1 gram of carbohydrate provides 4 calories.
  4. % Daily Value
    • Quick guide to % DV: The % DV section tells you the percent of each nutrient in a single serving, in terms of the daily-recommended amount. As a guide, if you want to consume less of a nutrient (such as saturated fat, cholesterol or sodium), choose foods with a lower % DV — 5 percent or less is low. If you want to consume more of a nutrient (such as fiber), seek foods with a higher % DV — 20 percent or more is high.

Remember that the information shown in these panels is based on 2,000 calories a day. That’s about 4 times more food than you are eating now.  The number of calories you require once you’ve reached your desired weight will be based upon your gender, age, height and weight.  For a 45-year-old male measuring 5’9” and 170 pounds doing light exercise 1-3 times a week would require about 2000 calories a day.  However, a 50-year-old female measuring 5’5” weighing 155 pounds doing little to no exercise would only require 1400 a day. 

We can't stress enough the importance of reading and understanding nutrition labels. They are often confusing and made that way intentionally. It's important you understand how to read them and take control of what enters your body.

For the ingredients label, remember items are listed in order of amount. The product contains more of the first ingredient listed than the last ingredient listed. Just for fun, next time you are in the grocery store, go to some of the foods you used to eat and see what ingredient are listed first.  Sugar? High fructose corn syrup? Might be surprising to you….

Happy, healthy eating!

Checkpoint Charlie

We’ve sent you a few of these daily emails about emotions, cravings and using the CRuSH technique to get through those tough moments. We’ve also talked about the stall week.  Today’s topic is a little more problematic.  It’s the dreaded yo-yo!

We have found that although we helped get agreement between your head and your heart on your first One on One Coaching session for your weight loss goal, sometimes, people reach a point where they feel “stuck.” The scale goes up and down around a certain weight but doesn’t seem to want to break through that barrier.

That’s what we call “Checkpoint Charlie.”

Checkpoint Charlie is almost always an emotional barrier and the CRUSH technique isn’t usually enough to help you break through it.  We’ll be watching for this on the SlenderProTracker.  We’ll see an “oscillation” around a specific weight and give you some “plateau breakers” (different meal suggestions).

Common checkpoints are 250 pounds, 200 pounds and going into the next lower “decade,” but they are actually very specific.

For example, you may experience something like the following (arbitrary weights):
Monday 201.5 lbs 
Tuesday 200.1 lbs 
Wednesday 199.8 lbs
Thursday 201.2 lb
Friday 200.1 lbs.

You can see that there is a roadblock to consistently losing weight below 200 lbs. This can and will be extremely frustrating!!

That’s when the frantic message comes in – “Help, I’m Stuck!!”

Don’t worry, help is on the way! During your Coaching session, we will discover the actual “Checkpoint Charlie” which is usually (but not always) 1/10 of a pound below the lowest weight you’ve achieved on the program, thus far.

Often, people will tell us that the emotional snapshot that comes up in the session is at a time when they were around the same weight they are now struggling to go beyond, but not always – it can be tricky.

Once that underlying emotional issue has been resolved, further weight loss continues.

Checkpoints can be challenging but learn to gently embrace them with patience and gratitude. There is healing to be received at these times.

Where Does the Fat Go?

Most people find this surprising, but when you burn fat, it is converted into carbon dioxide and water.

Current Research shows that during weight loss, 84 percent of the fat that is lost turns into carbon dioxide and leaves the body through the lungs, whereas the remaining 16 percent becomes water.

That means the lungs are the primary excretory organ for weight loss. The water formed may be excreted in the urine, feces, sweat, breath, tears or other bodily fluids.

Keep breathing and have a great day!

Variety is the Spice of Life

While we have a few vegetarians participate in our program most are meat eaters. Meat provides protein and protein provides amino acids – amino acids are the building blocks of life. It is very important to get your amino acids from a wide variety of different meats.

As you move into month two of the program, you will likely notice your daily weight loss slowing down gradually. This is normal, albeit not as much fun as the first week or two. More, now than ever, it is paramount that you change up your protein source constantly. The last thing you want to do is eat the same protein 4 meals in a row!

If you eat chicken breast for lunch on Monday, try not to eat chicken breast again until at least Wednesday. It’s ok to have red meat, too, but change up the cuts. For example, if you have sirloin on Monday, it is ok to have filet mignon on Tuesday. Mix in some wild caught fish as well – but, remember, Salmon steaks are not allowed, but smoked salmon is ok. Tuna steaks are not allowed, but Tuna packed in water is ok.

Vary your fruits and vegetables as well so you ensure a wide variety of vitamins and minerals from your diet. You are eating for life – make it fun and make it delicious!

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part II

Yesterday we learned about fat burning and fat storage mode and how turning one on turns the other off – just like drive and reverse in your car – Reciprocal Inhibition. The day before that we talked about momentum.

Today, I want to put those two together and give you a “why” for a couple aspects of our program.

First, the eating pattern is a “2-8-16 pattern.” 2 Meals in 8 hours, followed by 16 hours of fasting. You must eat your entire meal in one sitting instead of spreading it out over several hours. As soon as you start to eat, your body signals to stop “Fat Burning” and start “Digesting.” After you have eaten, your body will process the food, extract the calories and use some of them and store some of them. When that is completed, it goes back into “fat burning” of your abnormal fat. If you didn’t eat your apple at lunch, for example, and saved it for 3pm, then what would happen? The fat burning stops and digestion starts and “halt” goes your fat burning momentum between meals. Ugh…!

What about sugar free gum and breath mints or even eating free veggies as a snack? The same effect occurs. The act of chewing causes digestive enzymes to be released in the mouth which triggers the stop “Fat Burning” command and that signals start “Fat Storage.” Of course, it is a false start because there are no “net” calories to extract, so it’s not like chewing gum will cause you to gain weight, but the loss of momentum is what hurts your weight loss progress and that’s what we want to avoid.

If you feel you need to snack, drink some water, get busy on something for ten minutes and see if you still need that snack – normally the urge will be gone. Remember the CRuSH Technique as well….

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part I

Reciprocal inhibition is a fancy scientific term. I will give you an example of reciprocal inhibition – when you have your car in “Reverse” it can’t be in “Drive” at the same time.  In the body, when you flex your bicep muscle, the triceps muscle will relax –that’s reciprocal inhibition.

What the heck does this have to do with weight loss? Well, absolutely everything!

Reciprocal inhibition plays a part in fat burning and fat storage just like the transmission in your car. When you are in fat storage mode, you won’t be burning fat. And when your body is in fat burning mode, you can’t store it.

The foods you are eating on our plan in combination with the eating pattern and the SlenderPro drops and supplements puts you in FAT BURNING MODE. As soon as you stray from the program, fat burning stops.

Eating your normal meal of 4oz protein, 4oz or both vegetables and fruit will stop the fat burning process temporarily and for good reason. Your body will use the calories from your meal to replenish your reserve fat stores. That is necessary because those reserves are what runs your body over-night.  But as soon as they are used up, the body goes back into burning your abnormal fat stores which is the fat we don’t want

Do you feel hungry?

Going on a very low-calorie diet may be a bit of a shock for some people.  Most of us are used to eating all the time and way more than we need.  Learning to only eat small quantities can be tough.  The SlenderPro drops and support products will help keep your appetite at bay for the most part, and soon you’ll probably find that you will have a hard time eating all the food at each meal, but in the early days, it might be hard.

Here are some tips to help you out!

  • Add free vegetables to your meal in the form of a salad
  • Add free vegetables to your main course, like a stir fry using red cabbage, peppers, onions and celery
  • Have a few pickles or tomatoes with your meal.
  • Heat up some sauerkraut & green peppers with garlic, and pepper as a warm side dish
  • Have a bowl of Your SlenderPro Team’s “Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup with your meal

Your SlenderPro Team’s “Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup

  • 3 Red Bell Peppers – Cored and sectioned
  • ½ Purple Onion – cut in large chunks
  • 3 Cloves of Fresh Garlic
  • Can of Organic Diced Tomatoes
  • Water and Zero Calorie Non-Stick Cooking Spray
  • Dried Basil
  • Dried Rosemary
  • Pink Himalayan Salt 
  • Boiling Water

Toss red peppers, onions and garlic with Cooking Spray, Basil and Rosemary. Sprinkle with salt and roast in oven for 25 minutes at 425 degrees F.  Do not let vegetables blacken from the high heat, so turn often. When sufficiently roasted, remove from oven and put in high powered blender.  Add one can of diced tomatoes and boiling water.  Blend at high speed for about a minute.  

*Cooking alternative – instead of roasting, cook vegetables in a wok on the stove. It’s quicker and just as tasty!

Get creative with your food and have fun.  The variety will help you enjoy losing weight and there is never any reason to be hungry on this program.  But keep in mind, eating anything that isn’t on the approved foods list will cause hunger and cravings.  If in doubt, leave it out!

Do I have to eat all my food?

One of the most surprising questions I get is, “Do I have to eat all my food?” The answer is “YES!” People think they need to starve themselves to lose weight. Not true. On this program, you are eating a pound and a half of highly nutritious, nutrient dense food every day (plus all the free veggies you want!) If you think that skipping a meal or a meal component will result in more weight loss on the scale tomorrow morning, you will be unpleasantly surprised, most of the time. When you eat less than the prescribed daily allotment, your brain will over-ride the fat burning mode and put you into hard core storage mode because it thinks you are starving. Starvation mode is not the goal. Safe, rapid burning of your abnormal mode is the goal and is what will happen when you follow the plan.

So often we humans feel we can do things better by changing the plan. Please don’t do that with this program. Success leaves clues. Just do the little things every day and don’t stray. What could be easier?

It’s funny, but not surprising, how the people who stray from the plan don’t get the same results as the ones who just follow it. Trust me, I have a hard time with this because I am one of those who will challenge everything I am told. I have done that with this program and challenged it in every way imaginable. Guess what? It didn’t work as well as when I just followed it.

Please learn from our mistakes!

One question we get about water, “Is it possible to drink too much water?” The answer is yes. If you almost never drink water, then suddenly going to 120oz a day may cause problems – like stripping out your minerals – and you may start cramping.  If you are used to drinking water daily, then go ahead and increase your intake to 80 oz minimum. If you aren’t, start adding water every day to hit the minimum 80oz – 120 oz goal over the next week and a half or two weeks. Water is very important, but too much of anything can create problems!

One other question we get a lot after people read the SlenderPro manual is about oils, lotions and makeup. Check out the Resources tab of the SlenderProTracker for a comprehensive list of all approved oils and lotions. Oils, in general, interfere with the drops, so try to avoid them, both on your skin and on your food.

SLEEP AND WEIGHT LOSS

This ongoing topic of self-care is always super important.  We mentioned sleep yesterday but today we will dive a little deeper

According to health.gov, here are some benefits of proper sleep.

The Basics: Health Benefits

  1. Sleep helps reduce stress

If your body doesn’t get enough sleep, it can react by producing an elevated level of stress hormones, which are a natural result of today’s fast-paced lifestyles.  Deep and regular sleep can help prevent this

  1.  Sleep can improve your memory

Ever noticed that when you’re really tired it’s harder to remember things? Basically, this is your brain telling you that it’s not getting enough sleep. When you sleep well, your body may be resting but your brain is busy organizing and storing memories. So getting more quality sleep will help you remember and process things better.

  1. Sleep can lower your blood pressure

Higher blood pressure increases your chances of heart attacks and strokes, but getting plenty of restful sleep encourages a constant state of relaxation that can help reduce blood pressure and generally keep it under control.

  1. Sleep helps your body to fight back

While you’re sleeping your body is producing extra protein molecules that can strengthen your ability to fight infections. If you’re feeling a bit run down and don’t want it to turn into a full-blown cold, go to bed early and get lots of rest.

     5. Sleep can help you maintain your weight

Unfortunately, sleep won’t directly make you lose weight, but it can help you keep it under control by regulating the hormones that affect your appetite and reducing your cravings for high calorie foods.

6. Sleep puts you in a better mood

Lack of sleep can make us more agitated, so we’re more likely to snap at our boss or be grumpy with a loved one – neither of which is a good thing. The better you sleep, the better your ability to stay calm, controlled and reasonable.

7. Sleep could reduce your chances of diabetes

Some research studies have shown that not getting enough sleep may lead to type 2 diabetes by affecting how your body processes glucose. It’s not conclusive by any means, but it’s yet another indication of how important the benefits of sleep can be.

8. Sleep helps keep your heart healthy

A regular sleep pattern can help to lower the levels of stress and inflammation to your cardiovascular system, which in turn can reduce your chances of a heart condition.

9. Sleep can be a painkiller

If you’re suffering pain from a recent injury like a sprained ankle, getting plenty of sleep can actually make it hurt less. Many studies have shown a link between sleep loss and a lower pain threshold. Basically the more sleep you get, the less pain you might be in.

10. Sleep can make you smarter

Along with a great night’s sleep, grabbing a quick nap in the daytime can contribute towards making your brain more effective and productive. You won’t necessarily be answering all the questions on University Challenge, but you may well feel sharper, more attentive, and focused throughout the day.

If you’ve ever thought that sleep doesn’t matter all that much, think again, because it actually matters a great deal.

Sleep definitely has a huge impact on your health and wellbeing.  If you have difficulty sleeping, try some of these things…

  • Keep a regular bedtime and rising time.
  • Stay off of electronic devices at least one hour prior to bedtime.
  • Prepare yourself for the next day ahead of time to allow your mind to relax at night.
  • 30 minutes of reading or meditation prior to bedtime can help you fall asleep faster.
  • Sleep hypnosis helps many people.
  • Stop drinking caffeinated beverages early in the day
  • Start and end your day with gratitude.  Think about the good things in your life and how thankful you are for them.
  • Create a restful environment – fresh clean bedding, lavender oil, dim lighting, clean refreshing bedroom with everything in its place, etc.
  • Physical activity in your day also helps you sleep easier at night.
  • Keep a notepad next to your bed to write down those random thoughts that you may need to take care of the next day rather than continuing to keep those things on your mind.

If you have difficulty sleeping, sometimes melatonin helps many people fall and stay asleep.  It is all-natural and you can find it in many stores.  Check with your physician if you feel you may need something stronger for sleep disorders.

Here’s a “Mindfulness Exercise” For You to Try!

One of the challenges and therefore hesitations we get from people is giving up alcohol, sugar and dairy while on the program.

The first thing we say is, "It's only for a short bubble of time and you can do ANYTHING for this short a period!"

But there's still some hesitation. Once people are fully into the program and losing tons of weight and inches most are satisfied just going without these things. But at this point some may be tempted, thinking, "I've come so far, glass of wine or piece of chocolate won't hurt anything...."

Well, here's a shocker for you: One beer is like eating half a loaf of bread! In fact, the way the liver processes alcohol is such that your body will not only stop burning abnormal fat but start storing the calories from alcohol as abnormal fat!  Yeah, think about that before taking even a sip.

Okay, we're about to suggest something really shocking right now: break the rules a little.

Choose something that you have been missing – either an alcoholic beverage or treat. We are going to play a little game with it. This game is a “mindfulness exercise.”

Whatever the food or drink you choose, take the first little sip or bite and just hold it in your mouth. You will likely feel a “rush” start to take over you. These are your brain’s “old habit” pathways that are going to make you want to devour it and more.

Let’s Talk Nutrition Labels!         

Let’s talk about nutrition labels. Do you know how to read them?

Some people think they know, others only focus on one area and some people have never even given the nutrition label anything more than a glance!

While on the program, you really don’t need to be considering most labels because you are only eating from the approved foods list and are mostly fresh, whole foods. We don’t count calories on the plan, we weigh our food, as you know, but calories are listed on the label. The biggest misconception in the “diet” industry is that a calorie equals a calorie. This has never been true, is not true and will never be true. One calorie from alcohol and one calorie from ice cream and one calorie from chicken breast are all handled differently in the body and are therefore, not equal. If they were, you could only drink whiskey, eat no food and be totally healthy!

Let’s walk you through how to read the label and why it's vital to your success both now and in the future.

  1. Nutrition Facts
    • Start here: One of the most important steps, note the size of a single serving and how many servings are in a package. This tricks a lot of people. You may think a single drink or packaged food item is of course one serving, but many times there are many servings in one package. This can add up to disaster for you!
  2. Calories
    • Check total calories per serving: Look at the serving size and how many servings you're really consuming. If you double the servings you eat, you double the calories and nutrients, including the Percent Daily Value (% DV). Always do the math!
  3. Total Fat/Carbohydrates/Protein
    • Fat: Remember, you need to limit your total fat to no more than 56-78 grams a day — including no more than 16 grams of saturated fat, less than two grams of trans fat, and less than 300 mg cholesterol (these are all based on a 2,000 calorie diet).  On the SlenderPro Program you need to eat far less – fat to protein ratio is 7% fat to 93% protein – that’s 93% lean protein. It is possible to do the calculations using the ingredient label, but you would need to know that 1 gram of protein provides 4 calories and but 1 gram of fat provides 9 calories. For information sake, 1 gram of carbohydrate provides 4 calories.
  4. % Daily Value
    • Quick guide to % DV: The % DV section tells you the percent of each nutrient in a single serving, in terms of the daily-recommended amount. As a guide, if you want to consume less of a nutrient (such as saturated fat, cholesterol or sodium), choose foods with a lower % DV — 5 percent or less is low. If you want to consume more of a nutrient (such as fiber), seek foods with a higher % DV — 20 percent or more is high.

Remember that the information shown in these panels is based on 2,000 calories a day. That’s about 4 times more food than you are eating now.  The number of calories you require once you’ve reached your desired weight will be based upon your gender, age, height and weight.  For a 45-year-old male measuring 5’9” and 170 pounds doing light exercise 1-3 times a week would require about 2000 calories a day.  However, a 50-year-old female measuring 5’5” weighing 155 pounds doing little to no exercise would only require 1400 a day. 

We can't stress enough the importance of reading and understanding nutrition labels. They are often confusing and made that way intentionally. It's important you understand how to read them and take control of what enters your body.

For the ingredients label, remember items are listed in order of amount. The product contains more of the first ingredient listed than the last ingredient listed. Just for fun, next time you are in the grocery store, go to some of the foods you used to eat and see what ingredient are listed first.  Sugar? High fructose corn syrup? Might be surprising to you….

Happy, healthy eating!

Where Does the Fat Go?

Most people find this surprising, but when you burn fat, it is converted into carbon dioxide and water.

Current Research shows that during weight loss, 84 percent of the fat that is lost turns into carbon dioxide and leaves the body through the lungs, whereas the remaining 16 percent becomes water.

That means the lungs are the primary excretory organ for weight loss. The water formed may be excreted in the urine, feces, sweat, breath, tears or other bodily fluids.

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part II

Yesterday we learned about fat burning and fat storage mode and how turning one on turns the other off – just like drive and reverse in your car – Reciprocal Inhibition. The day before that we talked about momentum.

Today, I want to put those two together and give you a “why” for a couple aspects of our program.

First, the eating pattern is a “2-8-16 pattern.” 2 Meals in 8 hours, followed by 16 hours of fasting. You must eat your entire meal in one sitting instead of spreading it out over several hours. As soon as you start to eat, your body signals to stop “Fat Burning” and start “Digesting.” After you have eaten, your body will process the food, extract the calories and use some of them and store some of them. The fat burning stops and digestion starts and “halt” goes your fat burning momentum between meals. Ugh…!

The act of chewing causes digestive enzymes to be released in the mouth which triggers the stop “Fat Burning” command and that signals start “Fat Storage.” Of course, it is a false start because there are no “net” calories to extract, so it’s not like chewing gum will cause you to gain weight, but the loss of momentum is what hurts your weight loss progress and that’s what we want to avoid.

If you feel you need to snack, drink some water, get busy on something for ten minutes and see if you still need that snack – normally the urge will be gone. Remember the CRuSH Technique as well….

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part I

Reciprocal inhibition is a fancy scientific term. I will give you an example of reciprocal inhibition – when you have your car in “Reverse” it can’t be in “Drive” at the same time.  In the body, when you flex your bicep muscle, the triceps muscle will relax –that’s reciprocal inhibition.

What the heck does this have to do with weight loss? Well, absolutely everything!

Reciprocal inhibition plays a part in fat burning and fat storage just like the transmission in your car. When you are in fat storage mode, you won’t be burning fat. And when your body is in fat burning mode, you can’t store it.

The foods you are eating on our plan in combination with the eating pattern and the SlenderPro drops and supplements puts you in FAT BURNING MODE. As soon as you stray from the program, fat burning stops.

Eating your normal meal of 4oz protein, 4oz or both vegetables and fruit will stop the fat burning process temporarily and for good reason. Your body will use the calories from your meal to replenish your reserve fat stores. That is necessary because those reserves are what runs your body over-night.  But as soon as they are used up, the body goes back into burning your abnormal fat stores which is the fat we don’t want

Your SlenderPro Team’s “Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup

  • 3 Red Bell Peppers – Cored and sectioned
  • ½ Purple Onion – cut in large chunks
  • 3 Cloves of Fresh Garlic
  • Can of Organic Diced Tomatoes
  • Water and Zero Calorie Non-Stick Cooking Spray
  • Dried Basil
  • Dried Rosemary
  • Pink Himalayan Salt

Toss red peppers, onions and garlic with Cooking Spray, Basil and Rosemary. *Cooking alternative – instead of roasting, cook vegetables in a wok on the stove. It’s quicker and just as tasty!
