Do I have to eat all my food?

One of the most surprising questions I get is, “Do I have to eat all my food?” The answer is “YES!” People think they need to starve themselves to lose weight. Not true. On this program, you are eating a pound and a half of highly nutritious, nutrient dense food every day (plus all the free veggies you want!) If you think that skipping a meal or a meal component will result in more weight loss on the scale tomorrow morning, you will be unpleasantly surprised, most of the time. When you eat less than the prescribed daily allotment, your brain will over-ride the fat burning mode and put you into hard core storage mode because it thinks you are starving. Starvation mode is not the goal. Safe, rapid burning of your abnormal mode is the goal and is what will happen when you follow the plan.

So often we humans feel we can do things better by changing the plan. Please don’t do that with this program. Success leaves clues. Just do the little things every day and don’t stray. What could be easier?

It’s funny, but not surprising, how the people who stray from the plan don’t get the same results as the ones who just follow it. Trust me, I have a hard time with this because I am one of those who will challenge everything I am told. I have done that with this program and challenged it in every way imaginable. Guess what? It didn’t work as well as when I just followed it.

Please learn from our mistakes!

One question we get about water, “Is it possible to drink too much water?” The answer is yes. If you almost never drink water, then suddenly going to 120oz a day may cause problems – like stripping out your minerals – and you may start cramping.  If you are used to drinking water daily, then go ahead and increase your intake to 80 oz minimum. If you aren’t, start adding water every day to hit the minimum 80oz – 120 oz goal over the next week and a half or two weeks. Water is very important, but too much of anything can create problems!

One other question we get a lot after people read the SlenderPro manual is about oils, lotions and makeup. Check out the Resources tab of the SlenderProTracker for a comprehensive list of all approved oils and lotions. Oils, in general, interfere with the drops, so try to avoid them, both on your skin and on your food.

THE SKINNY ON EGGS

The skinny on eggs….

There are 78 calories in one egg (312 calories in four eggs).

There are only 17 calories in one egg white (51 calories in 3 egg whites).

Using one egg plus 3 egg whites to make scrambled eggs is only 129 calories and provides 16.8 grams of protein

Saving you 183 calories!!!

Egg substitutes (like Egg Beaters) are even better.  They are made completely from egg whites and taste just like regular scrambled eggs.

AHHHH ASPARAGUS

The Health Benefits of Asparagus

This giant veggie is one of the most nutritionally well-balanced vegetables -- high in folic acid and a good source of potassium, fiber, thiamin, and vitamins A, B6, and C. A 5-ounce serving provides 60% of the RDA for folic acid and is low in calories.

Doctors Favorite Asparagus Recipe

Clean and trim woody ends from asparagus stalks

Prepare air fryer or regular oven with directions below

In an air fryer use the french-fry setting (15 minutes at 400)

Spray the cooking grate with Pam spray

In oven, set temperature for 400

Line a baking sheet with parchment paper

Place asparagus in a single layer on cooking surface

Lightly spray asparagus with Pam spray

Season with Lemon Pepper seasoning or simply salt

Bake for 15 minutes

For a fresh kick, squeeze fresh lemon on asparagus just before serving

SLEEP AND WEIGHT LOSS

This ongoing topic of self-care is always super important.  We mentioned sleep yesterday but today we will dive a little deeper

According to health.gov, here are some benefits of proper sleep.

The Basics: Health Benefits

  1. Sleep helps reduce stress

If your body doesn’t get enough sleep, it can react by producing an elevated level of stress hormones, which are a natural result of today’s fast-paced lifestyles.  Deep and regular sleep can help prevent this

  1.  Sleep can improve your memory

Ever noticed that when you’re really tired it’s harder to remember things? Basically, this is your brain telling you that it’s not getting enough sleep. When you sleep well, your body may be resting but your brain is busy organizing and storing memories. So getting more quality sleep will help you remember and process things better.

  1. Sleep can lower your blood pressure

Higher blood pressure increases your chances of heart attacks and strokes, but getting plenty of restful sleep encourages a constant state of relaxation that can help reduce blood pressure and generally keep it under control.

  1. Sleep helps your body to fight back

While you’re sleeping your body is producing extra protein molecules that can strengthen your ability to fight infections. If you’re feeling a bit run down and don’t want it to turn into a full-blown cold, go to bed early and get lots of rest.

     5. Sleep can help you maintain your weight

Unfortunately, sleep won’t directly make you lose weight, but it can help you keep it under control by regulating the hormones that affect your appetite and reducing your cravings for high calorie foods.

6. Sleep puts you in a better mood

Lack of sleep can make us more agitated, so we’re more likely to snap at our boss or be grumpy with a loved one – neither of which is a good thing. The better you sleep, the better your ability to stay calm, controlled and reasonable.

7. Sleep could reduce your chances of diabetes

Some research studies have shown that not getting enough sleep may lead to type 2 diabetes by affecting how your body processes glucose. It’s not conclusive by any means, but it’s yet another indication of how important the benefits of sleep can be.

8. Sleep helps keep your heart healthy

A regular sleep pattern can help to lower the levels of stress and inflammation to your cardiovascular system, which in turn can reduce your chances of a heart condition.

9. Sleep can be a painkiller

If you’re suffering pain from a recent injury like a sprained ankle, getting plenty of sleep can actually make it hurt less. Many studies have shown a link between sleep loss and a lower pain threshold. Basically the more sleep you get, the less pain you might be in.

10. Sleep can make you smarter

Along with a great night’s sleep, grabbing a quick nap in the daytime can contribute towards making your brain more effective and productive. You won’t necessarily be answering all the questions on University Challenge, but you may well feel sharper, more attentive, and focused throughout the day.

If you’ve ever thought that sleep doesn’t matter all that much, think again, because it actually matters a great deal.

Sleep definitely has a huge impact on your health and wellbeing.  If you have difficulty sleeping, try some of these things…

  • Keep a regular bedtime and rising time.
  • Stay off of electronic devices at least one hour prior to bedtime.
  • Prepare yourself for the next day ahead of time to allow your mind to relax at night.
  • 30 minutes of reading or meditation prior to bedtime can help you fall asleep faster.
  • Sleep hypnosis helps many people.
  • Stop drinking caffeinated beverages early in the day
  • Start and end your day with gratitude.  Think about the good things in your life and how thankful you are for them.
  • Create a restful environment – fresh clean bedding, lavender oil, dim lighting, clean refreshing bedroom with everything in its place, etc.
  • Physical activity in your day also helps you sleep easier at night.
  • Keep a notepad next to your bed to write down those random thoughts that you may need to take care of the next day rather than continuing to keep those things on your mind.

If you have difficulty sleeping, sometimes melatonin helps many people fall and stay asleep.  It is all-natural and you can find it in many stores.  Check with your physician if you feel you may need something stronger for sleep disorders.

Pick Your Difficult!

Congratulations!!! You have made it into the next phase of the program.  The Maintenance/Locking phase begins today.  You will now be adding breakfast back into your diet and change your lunch and dinner by adding 2 additional oz of each food.  So instead of the 4/4/4 oz plan, you will now be eating 5-6oz. of each food for women and 6-7oz. of each food for men.  However, fruit will be 5 oz for both men and women.  And the optional approved bread product is still only one per day.  Breakfast should be no more than 300 calories.  A good recommended breakfast is egg white substitute omelet with free veggies, and turkey sausage.

Losing weight is difficult. Being overweight is difficult – Pick your difficult.

Let’s Talk Nutrition Labels!         

Let’s talk about nutrition labels. Do you know how to read them?

Some people think they know, others only focus on one area and some people have never even given the nutrition label anything more than a glance!

While on the program, you really don’t need to be considering most labels because you are only eating from the approved foods list and are mostly fresh, whole foods. We don’t count calories on the plan, we weigh our food, as you know, but calories are listed on the label. The biggest misconception in the “diet” industry is that a calorie equals a calorie. This has never been true, is not true and will never be true. One calorie from alcohol and one calorie from ice cream and one calorie from chicken breast are all handled differently in the body and are therefore, not equal. If they were, you could only drink whiskey, eat no food and be totally healthy!

Let’s walk you through how to read the label and why it's vital to your success both now and in the future.

  1. Nutrition Facts
    • Start here: One of the most important steps, note the size of a single serving and how many servings are in a package. This tricks a lot of people. You may think a single drink or packaged food item is of course one serving, but many times there are many servings in one package. This can add up to disaster for you!
  2. Calories
    • Check total calories per serving: Look at the serving size and how many servings you're really consuming. If you double the servings you eat, you double the calories and nutrients, including the Percent Daily Value (% DV). Always do the math!
  3. Total Fat/Carbohydrates/Protein
    • Fat: Remember, you need to limit your total fat to no more than 56-78 grams a day — including no more than 16 grams of saturated fat, less than two grams of trans fat, and less than 300 mg cholesterol (these are all based on a 2,000 calorie diet).  On the SlenderPro Program you need to eat far less – fat to protein ratio is 7% fat to 93% protein – that’s 93% lean protein. It is possible to do the calculations using the ingredient label, but you would need to know that 1 gram of protein provides 4 calories and but 1 gram of fat provides 9 calories. For information sake, 1 gram of carbohydrate provides 4 calories.
  4. % Daily Value
    • Quick guide to % DV: The % DV section tells you the percent of each nutrient in a single serving, in terms of the daily-recommended amount. As a guide, if you want to consume less of a nutrient (such as saturated fat, cholesterol or sodium), choose foods with a lower % DV — 5 percent or less is low. If you want to consume more of a nutrient (such as fiber), seek foods with a higher % DV — 20 percent or more is high.

Remember that the information shown in these panels is based on 2,000 calories a day. That’s about 4 times more food than you are eating now.  The number of calories you require once you’ve reached your desired weight will be based upon your gender, age, height and weight.  For a 45-year-old male measuring 5’9” and 170 pounds doing light exercise 1-3 times a week would require about 2000 calories a day.  However, a 50-year-old female measuring 5’5” weighing 155 pounds doing little to no exercise would only require 1400 a day. 

We can't stress enough the importance of reading and understanding nutrition labels. They are often confusing and made that way intentionally. It's important you understand how to read them and take control of what enters your body.

For the ingredients label, remember items are listed in order of amount. The product contains more of the first ingredient listed than the last ingredient listed. Just for fun, next time you are in the grocery store, go to some of the foods you used to eat and see what ingredient are listed first.  Sugar? High fructose corn syrup? Might be surprising to you….

Happy, healthy eating!

Where Does the Fat Go?

Most people find this surprising, but when you burn fat, it is converted into carbon dioxide and water.

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part I

Reciprocal inhibition is a fancy scientific term. I will give you an example of reciprocal inhibition – when you have your car in “Reverse” it can’t be in “Drive” at the same time.  In the body, when you flex your bicep muscle, the triceps muscle will relax –that’s reciprocal inhibition.

What the heck does this have to do with weight loss? Well, absolutely everything!

Reciprocal inhibition plays a part in fat burning and fat storage just like the transmission in your car. When you are in fat storage mode, you won’t be burning fat. And when your body is in fat burning mode, you can’t store it.

The foods you are eating on our plan in combination with the eating pattern and the SlenderPro drops and supplements puts you in FAT BURNING MODE. As soon as you stray from the program, fat burning stops.

Eating your normal meal of 4oz protein, 4oz or both vegetables and fruit will stop the fat burning process temporarily and for good reason. Your body will use the calories from your meal to replenish your reserve fat stores. That is necessary because those reserves are what runs your body over-night.  But as soon as they are used up, the body goes back into burning your abnormal fat stores which is the fat we don’t want

Have you added an exercise program to your routine? An easy way to add exercise to your day is with our ChiroBurst Training Program. The ChiroBurst Training Program consists of ten 30 second bursts with a 90 second rest period between bursts 3-4 days per week. This means that an entire workout is only 20 minutes with 5 minutes of actual exercise being performed each day. Your goal should be to work up to the point where you are able to perform 7 to 10 bursts cycles. I know this does not sound like a lot, however, since the exercise is being done at maximum effort, you may find that you are unable to perform more than 3-5 burst cycles that last only 10-15 seconds when you first start the ChiroBurst Training program. Additionally, you want to reach your maximum heart rate. This is determined by subtracting your age from 220. If you can reach your max heart rate in only a few bursts that is ok.

This high intensity exercise has been proven to boost your body’s growth hormone levels. This causes your body to burn fat for up to eight hours after you are done exercising. So while you are sitting on the couch or at your desk at work you are burning fat. If you were to do 3 burst training sessions a week you would be burning fat for up to 24 hours over the course of a week. This would occur with only 15-20 minutes of total weekly exercise time. This is compared to 3 hours of fat burning that is associated with 3 hours of aerobic exercise.

You do not want to ingest any carbohydrates (sugar) for 2 hours after a burst training session. Carbohydrates will increase a hormone called somatostatin which decreases your growth hormone induced fat burn. The ChiroThin Burst Training program has been designed specifically to aid you during the “Maintenance/Cycling Phases” of the ChiroThin Weight Loss Program. Additionally, it is a phenomenal workout program to continue once you have attained your weight loss goals.

By now you've watched the maintenance and cycling video and should now that you can introduce breakfast to your day. You can track your food intake as you did before, except now you eat 6 to 7 ounces of protein, veggies, and fruit; and you can double your Melba toast of breadsticks, three times a day. Ideally you're consuming the same amount of calories as your basal metabolic rate.

Your final body composition analysis has been downloaded to your Chirothin Tracker, and it notes your basal metoboic rate (BMR). This is the amount of calories you should be consuming daily. So you can either continue to count ounces of food, or switch to counting calories with the objective of eating your basal metabolic rate in calories each day. Either way, your objective is to eat an amount for your body to be comfortable that it is getting the right amount of food to sustain your current weight. This is how your body will soon adapt to the new you. It will learn that it's a safe new weight that will get an appropriate amount of food to live. And therefore, it doesn't have to worry about your weight, it can go on worrying about the rest of keeping you healthy. 

Neglecting to lock in your BMI and BMR results if the body continuing to fight to go back to it's original weight, and we don't want that do we?

Remeber that what you do today, your future self will thank you for in the future.

This is your first loading day. I am telling you that the two loading days may be the toughest part of your ten weeks. There is no need to log your food on the Tracker, but we need you to log your weight and water, including your weight, this morning. If you haven't already logged your morning weight, please log in now and do so. Also, please count calories using your journal or the MyFitnessPal free app. You need to hit 2500 calories over your BMR, usually 4000 or above for women and 5000 for men. If you don't recall how many calories, we instructed you to eat, make sure to hit 4,000 or 5,000 for women and men, respectively.

Today you should take seven drops three times a day, seven hours apart. You also should take digestive enzymes. Do not start taking AGGR until day 12; for Prime and Premier package patients, do not wear your Livewave patches until day four. 

So why do we have you load? There are a few reasons, but they all lead to improved weight loss success in our ChiroThin program. As soon as you restrict your food intake to the losing phase requirements of the program, it's very alarming to the body. Your body says, "What's going on here? There must be a shortage of food supply, so I better start storing away whatever I can in my fat cells to make it through this shortage, so I don't die of starvation." This is what's called Starvation Mode. So, unless there's a way to bypass the Starvation Mode, it's very difficult to lose weight. Lucky for you, there is a way, which is one major reason you must load properly.

  • To bypass Starvation Mode, you need to increase your fat reserves and show the body that you're feasting while preparing for a famine. During a feast time, your body begins to store fat, which fills your healthy fat stores, which need to be filled at the start of the program for the body to feel comfortable releasing fat as you enter the losing phase of the program. 
  • Leptin is a hormone produced by fat cells in your body. It tells your brain when you have enough fat stored. It's what keeps us from starving or overeating in our current state. By loading, leptin is elevated, decreasing your appetite and increasing fat metabolism, which helps you get through the first couple of days of the diet.  That quick leptin buzz is responsible for boosting metabolism after overeating. And in addition to regulating hunger and metabolism, this hormone may increase motivation.

How to practice MINDFUL EATING

Eating while you’re also doing other things—such as watching TV, driving, or playing with your phone—can prevent you from fully enjoying your food. Since your mind is elsewhere, you may not feel satisfied or continue eating even though you’re no longer hungry. Eating more mindfully can help focus your mind on your food and the pleasure of a meal and curb overeating.

  • Eat your meals in a calm place with no distractions, aside from any dining companions.
  • Before you start to eat, take a moment to consider what it took to produce your meal, from the farmer to the grocer to the cook.
  • Try eating with your non-dominant hand or using chopsticks instead of a knife and fork. Eating in such a non-familiar way can slow down how fast you eat and ensure your mind stays focused on your food.
  • Allow yourself enough time not to have to rush your meal. Set a timer for 20 minutes and pace yourself so you spend at least that much time eating.
  • Take small bites and chew them well, taking time to notice the different flavors and textures of each mouthful.
  • Put your utensils down between bites. Take time to consider how you feel—hungry, satiated—before picking up your utensils again.
  • Try to stop eating before you are full. It takes time for the signal to reach your brain that you’ve had enough. Don’t feel obligated to always clean your plate.
  • When you’ve finished your food, take a few moments to assess if you’re really still hungry before opting for an extra serving or dessert.

Let’s talk about emotional hunger and how to REPLACE it!

  • Emotional hunger comes on suddenly.  Physical hunger, on the other hand, comes on more gradually.
  • Emotional hunger craves specific comfort foods. Emotional hunger craves junk food or sugary snacks that provide an instant rush.
  • Emotional hunger isn’t satisfied once you’re full. You keep wanting more and more, often eating until you’re uncomfortably stuffed. Physical hunger feels satisfied when your stomach is full.
  • Emotional hunger isn’t located in the stomach. Rather than a growling belly or a pang in your stomach, you feel your hunger as a craving you can’t get out of your head.
  • Emotional hunger often leads to regret, guilt, or shame. When you eat to satisfy physical hunger, you’re unlikely to feel guilty or ashamed.

Triggers

  • Stuffing emotions 
  • Boredom or feelings of emptiness 
  • Childhood habits 
  • Social influences 
  • Stress 

Combat emotional eating with these tricks

  • If you’re depressed or lonely, call someone who always makes you feel better, play with your dog or cat, or look at a favorite photo or cherished memento.
  • If you’re anxious, expend your nervous energy by dancing to your favorite song, squeezing a stress ball, or taking a brisk walk.
  • If you’re exhausted, treat yourself with a hot cup of tea, take a bath, light some scented candles, or wrap yourself in a warm blanket.
  • If you’re bored, read a good book, watch a comedy show, explore the outdoors, or turn to an activity you enjoy (woodworking, playing the guitar, shooting hoops, scrapbooking, etc.).

Day 62: Locking Phase  

Here’s a “Mindfulness Exercise” For You to Try!

One of the challenges and therefore hesitations we get from people is giving up alcohol, sugar and dairy while on the program.

The first thing we say is, "It's only for a short bubble of time and you can do ANYTHING for this short a period!"

But there's still some hesitation. Once people are fully into the program and losing tons of weight and inches most are satisfied just going without these things. But at this point some may be tempted, thinking, "I've come so far, glass of wine or piece of chocolate won't hurt anything...."

Well, here's a shocker for you: One beer is like eating half a loaf of bread! In fact, the way the liver processes alcohol is such that your body will not only stop burning abnormal fat but start storing the calories from alcohol as abnormal fat!  Yeah, think about that before taking even a sip.

Okay, we're about to suggest something really shocking right now: break the rules a little.

Choose something that you have been missing – either an alcoholic beverage or treat. We are going to play a little game with it. This game is a “mindfulness exercise.”

Whatever the food or drink you choose, take the first little sip or bite and just hold it in your mouth. You will likely feel a “rush” start to take over you. These are your brain’s “old habit” pathways that are going to make you want to devour it and more. 

RESIST the urge to swallow at that moment.

One calorie from alcohol and one calorie from ice cream and one calorie from chicken breast are all handled differently in the body and are therefore, not equal. If they were, you could only drink whiskey, eat no food and be totally healthy!

Let’s walk you through how to read the label and why it's vital to your success both now and in the future.

  1. Nutrition Facts
    • Start here: One of the most important steps, note the size of a single serving and how many servings are in a package. This tricks a lot of people. You may think a single drink or packaged food item is of course one serving, but many times there are many servings in one package. This can add up to disaster for you!
  2. Calories
    • Check total calories per serving: Look at the serving size and how many servings you're really consuming. If you double the servings you eat, you double the calories and nutrients, including the Percent Daily Value (% DV). Always do the math!
  3. Total Fat/Carbohydrates/Protein
    • Fat: Remember, you need to limit your total fat to no more than 56-78 grams a day — including no more than 16 grams of saturated fat, less than two grams of trans fat, and less than 300 mg cholesterol (these are all based on a 2,000 calorie diet).  On the ChiroThin Program you need to eat far less – fat to protein ratio is 7% fat to 93% protein – that’s 93% lean protein. It is possible to do the calculations using the ingredient label, but you would need to know that 1 gram of protein provides 4 calories and but 1 gram of fat provides 9 calories. For information sake, 1 gram of carbohydrate provides 4 calories.
  4. % Daily Value
    • Quick guide to % DV: The % DV section tells you the percent of each nutrient in a single serving, in terms of the daily-recommended amount. As a guide, if you want to consume less of a nutrient (such as saturated fat, cholesterol or sodium), choose foods with a lower % DV — 5 percent or less is low. If you want to consume more of a nutrient (such as fiber), seek foods with a higher % DV — 20 percent or more is high.

Remember that the information shown in these panels is based on 2,000 calories a day. That’s about 4 times more food than you are eating now.  The number of calories you require once you’ve reached your desired weight will be based upon your gender, age, height and weight.  For a 45-year-old male measuring 5’9” and 170 pounds doing light exercise 1-3 times a week would require about 2000 calories a day.  However, a 50-year-old female measuring 5’5” weighing 155 pounds doing little to no exercise would only require 1400 a day. 

We can't stress enough the importance of reading and understanding nutrition labels. They are often confusing and made that way intentionally. It's important you understand how to read them and take control of what enters your body.

For the ingredients label, remember items are listed in order of amount. The product contains more of the first ingredient listed than the last ingredient listed. Just for fun, next time you are in the grocery store, go to some of the foods you used to eat and see what ingredient are listed first.  Sugar? High fructose corn syrup? Might be surprising to you….

Happy, healthy eating!

Where Does the Fat Go?

Most people find this surprising, but when you burn fat, it is converted into carbon dioxide and water.

That means the lungs are the primary excretory organ for weight loss. The water formed may be excreted in the urine, feces, sweat, breath, tears or other bodily fluids.

Day 18: Losing Phase

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part II

Yesterday we learned about fat burning and fat storage mode and how turning one on turns the other off – just like drive and reverse in your car – Reciprocal Inhibition. The day before that we talked about momentum.

Today, I want to put those two together and give you a “why” for a couple aspects of our program.

First, the eating pattern is a “2-8-16 pattern.” 2 Meals in 8 hours, followed by 16 hours of fasting. You must eat your entire meal in one sitting instead of spreading it out over several hours. What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part I

Reciprocal inhibition is a fancy scientific term. I will give you an example of reciprocal inhibition – when you have your car in “Reverse” it can’t be in “Drive” at the same time.  In the body, when you flex your bicep muscle, the triceps muscle will relax –that’s reciprocal inhibition.

What the heck does this have to do with weight loss? Well, absolutely everything!

Reciprocal inhibition plays a part in fat burning and fat storage just like the transmission in your car. When you are in fat storage mode, you won’t be burning fat. And when your body is in fat burning mode, you can’t store it.

The foods you are eating on our plan in combination with the eating pattern and the ChiroThin drops and supplements puts you in FAT BURNING MODE. As soon as you stray from the program, fat burning stops.

  • 3 Cloves of Fresh Garlic
  • Can of Organic Diced Tomatoes
  • Water and Zero Calorie Non-Stick Cooking Spray

  • Download the "My Fitness Pal" app onto your smart phone to help you count your calories on loading days.
  • There is no specific water requirement on the two Loading Days.
  • Discontinue all vitamins, minerals and supplements (unless prescribed by your medical doctor).
  • Put the ice pack in the freezer for your urine sample. (For those doing the 24 hour urine test).
  • When taking your drops – drop them one at a time into a spoon to ensure you don’t run out. There is 7-1/2 weeks of drops in each bottle with a calibrated dropper to ensure you have enough for your round. Be very mindful of this detail.
  • Set “drops” alarm on your phone to remind you to take your drops (7 drops each dose) at 7am, 2pm and 9pm. (It doesn’t have to be these exact times, but there should be about 7 hours between doses).
  • Take 7 drops of the ChiroThin Formula (3 x a day) – hold the drops under your tongue for 60 seconds and then swallow. Wait 10 minutes before eating or drinking.
  • Consume 5000 calories today – but don’t throw up!

Helpful Loading Day Tips

  • You must remember to take your drops while loading! This is necessary to start unlocking your abnormal fat. You start taking your drops on your loading days and every day on the losing phase - you won't be taking drops on your locking phase, but that will come later.
  • There are two days of loading and you MUST that you hit the 5000 calorie mark – this is MASSIVELY IMPORTANT because it spikes your metabolism while you are taking your ChiroThin drops. This sets your metabolism at a very high rate for your round as we turn you into a fat burning machine! 
  • Enjoy your favorite foods or things you know you'll crave - pizza, milk and cookies, nachos, peanut butter, bread, candy bars, etc. If you indulge on your "crave" items now it will be easier to resist over the losing phase and for a lifetime!
  • Graze all day. Don't try to cram 5000 calories into three meals. Snacks like peanut butter, nuts, chips, cookies, cakes, etc. are great, but high fat foods are the BEST. Avocados, coconut oil, butter, whipping cream and nut butters are great examples. If you find yourself really struggling to eat all the calories, try to consume some through liquids like soda, sweet tea, juice, a milk shake or even a few alcoholic beverages.
  • Plan ahead. It's important to plan your day of eating; it will make it possible for you to reach the 5000-calorie total. Plan your day from breakfast, snacks, lunch and everything in between! Planning will also be key to your success during the losing phase, so it's good practice.

Day 62: Locking Phase  

Here’s a “Mindfulness Exercise” For You to Try!

One of the challenges and therefore hesitations we get from people is giving up alcohol, sugar and dairy while on the program.

The first thing we say is, "It's only for a short bubble of time and you can do ANYTHING for this short a period!"

But there's still some hesitation. Once people are fully into the program and losing tons of weight and inches most are satisfied just going without these things. But at this point some may be tempted, thinking, "I've come so far, glass of wine or piece of chocolate won't hurt anything...."

Well, here's a shocker for you: One beer is like eating half a loaf of bread! In fact, the way the liver processes alcohol is such that your body will not only stop burning abnormal fat but start storing the calories from alcohol as abnormal fat!  Yeah, think about that before taking even a sip.

Okay, we're about to suggest something really shocking right now: break the rules a little.

Choose something that you have been missing – either an alcoholic beverage or treat. We are going to play a little game with it. This game is a “mindfulness exercise.”

Whatever the food or drink you choose, take the first little sip or bite and just hold it in your mouth. You will likely feel a “rush” start to take over you. These are your brain’s “old habit” pathways that are going to make you want to devour it and more. 

RESIST the urge to swallow at that moment.

Hold it in your mouth and watch as the “rush” starts to subside. Now, experience the taste of it on your tongue.

Do you even like it? Does it taste the same? I’ll bet it’s somehow different. That’s the transformation of your relationship with food and drink that is occurring within you on this program.

Day 36: Losing Phase

Let’s Talk Nutrition Labels!         

Let’s talk about nutrition labels. Do you know how to read them?

Some people think they know, others only focus on one area and some people have never even given the nutrition label anything more than a glance!

While on the program, you really don’t need to be considering most labels because you are only eating from the approved foods list and are mostly fresh, whole foods. We don’t count calories on the plan, we weigh our food, as you know, but calories are listed on the label. The biggest misconception in the “diet” industry is that a calorie equals a calorie. This has never been true, is not true and will never be true. One calorie from alcohol and one calorie from ice cream and one calorie from chicken breast are all handled differently in the body and are therefore, not equal. If they were, you could only drink whiskey, eat no food and be totally healthy!

Let’s walk you through how to read the label and why it's vital to your success both now and in the future.

  1. Nutrition Facts
    • Start here: One of the most important steps, note the size of a single serving and how many servings are in a package. This tricks a lot of people. You may think a single drink or packaged food item is of course one serving, but many times there are many servings in one package. This can add up to disaster for you!
  2. Calories
    • Check total calories per serving: Look at the serving size and how many servings you're really consuming. If you double the servings you eat, you double the calories and nutrients, including the Percent Daily Value (% DV). Always do the math!
  3. Total Fat/Carbohydrates/Protein
    • Fat: Remember, you need to limit your total fat to no more than 56-78 grams a day — including no more than 16 grams of saturated fat, less than two grams of trans fat, and less than 300 mg cholesterol (these are all based on a 2,000 calorie diet).  On the ChiroThin Program you need to eat far less – fat to protein ratio is 7% fat to 93% protein – that’s 93% lean protein. It is possible to do the calculations using the ingredient label, but you would need to know that 1 gram of protein provides 4 calories and but 1 gram of fat provides 9 calories. For information sake, 1 gram of carbohydrate provides 4 calories.
  4. % Daily Value
    • Quick guide to % DV: The % DV section tells you the percent of each nutrient in a single serving, in terms of the daily-recommended amount. As a guide, if you want to consume less of a nutrient (such as saturated fat, cholesterol or sodium), choose foods with a lower % DV — 5 percent or less is low. If you want to consume more of a nutrient (such as fiber), seek foods with a higher % DV — 20 percent or more is high.

Remember that the information shown in these panels is based on 2,000 calories a day. That’s about 4 times more food than you are eating now.  The number of calories you require once you’ve reached your desired weight will be based upon your gender, age, height and weight.  For a 45-year-old male measuring 5’9” and 170 pounds doing light exercise 1-3 times a week would require about 2000 calories a day.  However, a 50-year-old female measuring 5’5” weighing 155 pounds doing little to no exercise would only require 1400 a day. 

We can't stress enough the importance of reading and understanding nutrition labels. They are often confusing and made that way intentionally. It's important you understand how to read them and take control of what enters your body.

For the ingredients label, remember items are listed in order of amount. The product contains more of the first ingredient listed than the last ingredient listed. Just for fun, next time you are in the grocery store, go to some of the foods you used to eat and see what ingredient are listed first.  Sugar? High fructose corn syrup? Might be surprising to you….

 

Happy, healthy eating!

Where Does the Fat Go?

Most people find this surprising, but when you burn fat, it is converted into carbon dioxide and water.

Day 18: Losing Phase

What the heck is “Reciprocal Inhibition?” – Part II

Yesterday we learned about fat burning and fat storage mode and how turning one on turns the other off – just like drive and reverse in your car – Reciprocal Inhibition. The day before that we talked about momentum.

Today, I want to put those two together and give you a “why” for a couple aspects of our program.

First, the eating pattern is a “2-8-16 pattern.” 2 Meals in 8 hours, followed by 16 hours of fasting. You must eat your entire meal in one sitting instead of spreading it out over several hours. As soon as you start to eat, your body signals to stop “Fat Burning” and start “Digesting.” After you have eaten, your body will process the food, extract the calories and use some of them and store some of them. When that is completed, it goes back into “fat burning” of your abnormal fat. If you didn’t eat your apple at lunch, for example, and saved it for 3pm, then what would happen? The fat burning stops and digestion starts and “halt” goes your fat burning momentum between meals. Ugh…!

What about sugar free gum and breath mints or even eating free veggies as a snack? The same effect occurs. The act of chewing causes digestive enzymes to be released in the mouth which triggers the stop “Fat Burning” command and that signals start “Fat Storage.” Of course, it is a false start because there are no “net” calories to extract, so it’s not like chewing gum will cause you to gain weight, but the loss of momentum is what hurts your weight loss progress and that’s what we want to avoid.

If you feel you need to snack, drink some water, get busy on something for ten minutes and see if you still need that snack – normally the urge will be gone. Remember the CRuSH Technique as well….

You’re doing great!

Reciprocal inhibition is a fancy scientific term. I will give you an example of reciprocal inhibition – when you have your car in “Reverse” it can’t be in “Drive” at the same time.  In the body, when you flex your bicep muscle, the triceps muscle will relax –that’s reciprocal inhibition.

What the heck does this have to do with weight loss? Well, absolutely everything!

Reciprocal inhibition plays a part in fat burning and fat storage just like the transmission in your car. When you are in fat storage mode, you won’t be burning fat. And when your body is in fat burning mode, you can’t store it.

The foods you are eating on our plan in combination with the eating pattern and the ChiroThin drops and supplements puts you in FAT BURNING MODE. As soon as you stray from the program, fat burning stops.

Eating your normal meal of 4oz protein, 4oz or both vegetables and fruit will stop the fat burning process temporarily and for good reason. Your body will use the calories from your meal to replenish your reserve fat stores. That is necessary because those reserves are what runs your body over-night.  But as soon as they are used up, the body goes back into burning your abnormal fat stores which is the fat we don’t want

Keep burning!

  • Have a bowl of Dr. John’s “Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup with your meal

Dr. John’s “Free” Roasted Red Pepper and Tomato Soup

  • 3 Red Bell Peppers – Cored and sectioned
  • ½ Purple Onion – cut in large chunks
  • 3 Cloves of Fresh Garlic
  • Can of Organic Diced Tomatoes
  • Water and Zero Calorie Non-Stick Cooking Spray
  • Dried Basil
  • Dried Rosemary
  • Pink Himalayan Salt 
  • Boiling Water

Toss red peppers, onions and garlic with Cooking Spray, Basil and Rosemary. We're talking about nutrition labels. Do you know how to read them?

Some people think they know, others only focus on one area and some people have never even given the nutrition label a thought!

We're going to walk you through how to read the label and why it's vital to your success now and especially once you're done with the weight loss program.

Start here: One of the most important steps, note the size of a single serving and how many servings are in a package. This tricks a lot of people. You may think a single drink or packaged food item is of course one serving, but many times it's multiple servings in one package. This can add up to disaster for you!

Check total calories per serving: Look at the serving size and how many servings you're really consuming. If you double the servings you eat, you double the calories and nutrients, including the Percent Daily Value (% DV). So always do the math!

Limit these nutrients: Remember, you need to limit your total fat to no more than 56-78 grams a day — including no more than 16 grams of saturated fat, less than two grams of trans fat, and less than 300 mg cholesterol (for a 2,000 calorie diet).

Get enough of these nutrients. Make sure you get 100 percent of the fiber, vitamins and other nutrients you need every day.

Quick guide to % DV: The % DV section tells you the percent of each nutrient in a single serving, in terms of the daily-recommended amount. As a guide, if you want to consume less of a nutrient (such as saturated fat, cholesterol or sodium), choose foods with a lower % DV — 5 percent or less is low. If you want to consume more of a nutrient (such as fiber), seek foods with a higher % DV — 20 percent or more is high.

Remember that the information shown in these panels is based on 2,000 calories a day.

We can't stress enough the importance of reading and understanding nutrition labels. They are often confusing and made that way purposefully so. It's important you understand how to read them and take control of what enters your body.

For the ingredients label, remember items are listed in order of amount. So the first ingredient listed is more concentrated in the product than, say, the last ingredient listed.

If you really want to avoid labels you can stick with actual food and you don't have to worry. Veggies are veggies for example.

Happy eating!
